statement: Let G be the undirected multigraph whose vertices are 0,...,n-1 and which has one edge between edges[j][0] and edges[j][1] of weight edges[j][2] for every j with 0 <= j < len(edges). For a walk W in G, let cost(W) be the bitwise AND of the weights of all edges traversed by W, counting repetitions. Whenever the function returns a result r, it holds that len(r) = len(query) and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(query), writing s = query[i][0] and t = query[i][1], if there exists a walk from s to t in G then r[i] is the minimum of cost(W) over all walks W from s to t in G, and if there is no walk from s to t in G then r[i] = -1.
preconditions: n is an integer with 2 <= n <= 100000. len(edges) <= 100000, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(edges), len(edges[j]) = 3, 0 <= edges[j][0] <= n-1, 0 <= edges[j][1] <= n-1, edges[j][0] != edges[j][1], and 0 <= edges[j][2] <= 100000. Also 1 <= len(query) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(query), len(query[i]) = 2, 0 <= query[i][0] <= n-1, 0 <= query[i][1] <= n-1, and query[i][0] != query[i][1].
